meta.title: Hindi Alphabet (Devanagari)
meta.subtitle: 59 letters and signs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Devanagari script in which Hindi is written: 59 notes, in the traditional order — the eleven vowels, the four signs that sit on them, the thirty-three consonants row by row, the two flapped letters Hindi added (ड़, ढ़), the four joined letters every primer teaches with the alphabet (क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ, श्र) and the five dotted (nukta) letters of words from Persian, Arabic and English. The first deck of the Hindi collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Each vowel is shown alone and as the sign it becomes after a consonant, written on क (आ · का), since the sign is what a reader meets most. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — the breathy consonants (kh, gh, bh …), the curled-back retroflex row (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ) against the soft dental t and d — the card says what to do with the tongue or the breath instead. Sources: the standard description of modern standard Hindi; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: अ
fields.Sound: a · a short, neutral "a", like the a of about; every consonant carries it unless a sign says otherwise, so it has no sign of its own

fields.Name: आ
fields.Sound: ā · "a" as in father, long

fields.Name: इ
fields.Sound: i · "i" as in bit, short; its sign is written BEFORE the consonant it follows in speech

fields.Name: ई
fields.Sound: ī · "ee" as in see, long

fields.Name: उ
fields.Sound: u · "u" as in put, short

fields.Name: ऊ
fields.Sound: ū · "oo" as in food, long

fields.Name: ऋ
fields.Sound: ŕ · said "ri" as in rip; found in words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: ए
fields.Sound: e · like the a of cake, but one pure vowel, without the glide into "ee"

fields.Name: ऐ
fields.Sound: ai · in standard Hindi like the a of bat held long, between the e of bed and the a of bad — not the "ai" of aisle

fields.Name: ओ
fields.Sound: o · like the o of go, but one pure vowel, without the glide into "oo"

fields.Name: औ
fields.Sound: au · like the aw of law — not the "ow" of cow

fields.Name: अनुस्वार
fields.Sound: ṃ · anusvāra, the dot above: a nasal before the next consonant, said as the n or m that suits it (n before d, m before b)

fields.Name: चंद्रबिंदु
fields.Sound: chandrabindu, the moon and dot: the vowel is said through the nose, as in French bon; often written as a plain dot instead

fields.Name: विसर्ग
fields.Sound: ḥ · visarga, the two dots: a breath of "h" after the vowel, in a few words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: हलंत
fields.Sound: halant (virāma), the stroke below: the consonant has NO vowel after it; usually two such consonants are joined into one shape instead (क् + य = क्य)

fields.Name: क
fields.Sound: ka · "k" as in skin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: ख
fields.Sound: kha · "k" with a strong puff of breath, as in kit said firmly

fields.Name: ग
fields.Sound: ga · "g" as in go

fields.Name: घ
fields.Sound: gha · "g" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of doghouse

fields.Name: ङ
fields.Sound: ṅa · "ng" as in sing; never starts a word, and is usually written as the dot above (anusvāra) instead

fields.Name: च
fields.Sound: ca · "ch" as in church, but with no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: छ
fields.Sound: cha · "ch" with a strong puff of breath, as in the middle of church-hill

fields.Name: ज
fields.Sound: ja · "j" as in jam

fields.Name: झ
fields.Sound: jha · "j" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of hedgehog

fields.Name: ञ
fields.Sound: ña · "ny" as in canyon; rare, and usually written as the dot above instead

fields.Name: ट
fields.Sound: ṭa · a "t" made with the tip of the tongue curled back to the roof of the mouth (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the t of top

fields.Name: ठ
fields.Sound: ṭha · the curled-back (retroflex) t, with a strong puff of breath

fields.Name: ड
fields.Sound: ḍa · a "d" made with the tongue tip curled back (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the d of dog

fields.Name: ढ
fields.Sound: ḍha · the curled-back (retroflex) d, followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: ण
fields.Sound: ṇa · an "n" made with the tongue tip curled back (retroflex); rarely starts a word

fields.Name: त
fields.Sound: ta · a soft "t" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental), as in French or Spanish; no puff of breath

fields.Name: थ
fields.Sound: tha · the dental t with a strong puff of breath — not the "th" of thin

fields.Name: द
fields.Sound: da · a soft "d" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental) — not the "th" of this

fields.Name: ध
fields.Sound: dha · the dental d followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: न
fields.Sound: na · "n" as in no

fields.Name: प
fields.Sound: pa · "p" as in spin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: फ
fields.Sound: pha · "p" with a strong puff of breath; many speakers say it as "f"

fields.Name: ब
fields.Sound: ba · "b" as in bat

fields.Name: भ
fields.Sound: bha · "b" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of clubhouse

fields.Name: म
fields.Sound: ma · "m" as in man

fields.Name: य
fields.Sound: ya · "y" as in yes

fields.Name: र
fields.Sound: ra · a tapped "r", one flick of the tongue, as in Spanish pero

fields.Name: ल
fields.Sound: la · "l" as in leaf, said with the tongue forward

fields.Name: व
fields.Sound: va · between "v" and "w": the lower lip only lightly touches the teeth

fields.Name: श
fields.Sound: śa · "sh" as in ship

fields.Name: ष
fields.Sound: ṣa · a second "sh", written in words from Sanskrit; in Hindi said just like श

fields.Name: स
fields.Sound: sa · "s" as in sun

fields.Name: ह
fields.Sound: ha · "h" as in hand, often voiced and breathy

fields.Name: ड़
fields.Sound: ṛa · a flap: the tongue tip curls back and flicks forward against the roof of the mouth, a sound between d and r; never starts a word

fields.Name: ढ़
fields.Sound: ṛha · the same flap followed by a breathy h; never starts a word
fields.Example: पढ़नाpaṛhnāto read, to study

fields.Name: क्ष
fields.Sound: kṣa · a joined letter, क् + ष, said "ksh"

fields.Name: त्र
fields.Sound: tra · a joined letter, त् + र, said "tr" with the soft dental t

fields.Name: ज्ञ
fields.Sound: jña · a joined letter, ज् + ञ, said "gy" in Hindi

fields.Name: श्र
fields.Sound: śra · a joined letter, श् + र, said "shr"

fields.Name: ज़
fields.Sound: za · "z" as in zoo — ज with a dot (nukta) below; many speakers say it as ज

fields.Name: फ़
fields.Sound: fa · "f" as in fan — फ with a dot (nukta) below

fields.Name: क़
fields.Sound: qa · a "k" made further back, in the throat (from Arabic); many speakers say it as क

fields.Name: ख़
fields.Sound: xa · like the ch of Scottish loch — ख with a dot (nukta) below

fields.Name: ग़
fields.Sound: ġa · a gargled "g", like the French r — ग with a dot (nukta) below
